questions.text:
A five-stage pipeline has stage delays of 150, 120, 150, 160 and 140 nanoseconds. The registers that are used between the pipeline stages have a delay of 5 nanoseconds each.
The total time to execute 100 independent instructions on this pipeline, assuming there are no pipeline stalls, is _______ nanoseconds.
questions.solution:
Clock cycle = slowest stage + register delay = 160 + 5 = 165 ns.
Cycles for 100 instructions on 5 stages = 5 + 100 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 104.

Time = 104 [latex]\times[/latex] 165 = 17160 ns

Answer: 17160

questions.text:
Consider a computer system with a byte-addressable primary memory of size [latex]2^{32} \text{ bytes}[/latex]. Assume the computer system has a direct-mapped cache of size [latex]32 KB (1 KB = 2^{10} \text{ bytes})[/latex], and each cache block is of size 64 bytes.
The size of the tag field is __________ bits.
questions.solution:
Lines = 32 KB / 64 B = 512 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 9 index bits. Offset = 6 bits.

Tag = 32 [latex]-[/latex] 9 [latex]-[/latex] 6 = 17 bits

Answer: 17

questions.text: One instruction tries to write an operand before it is written by previous instruction. This may lead to a dependency called
questions.solution:
A later instruction writing an operand before an earlier instruction writes it is a write after write (WAW) hazard, also called output dependency.

Answer: Output dependency

questions.text: How many total bits are required for a direct-mapped cache with 128 KB of data and 1 word block size, assuming a 32-bit address and 1 word size of 4 bytes?
questions.solution:
128 KB / 4 B = [latex]2^{15}[/latex] blocks (one word each).
Address: offset 2 bits, index 15 bits, tag = 32 [latex]-[/latex] 17 = 15 bits.

Bits per line = 32 (data) + 15 (tag) + 1 (valid) = 48.
Total = [latex]2^{15}\times48=1.5\times2^{20}[/latex] bits = 1.5 Mbits

Answer: 1.5 Mbits

questions.text: A magnetic disk has 100 cylinders, each with 10 tracks of 10 sectors. If each sector contains 128 bytes, what is the maximum capacity of the disk in kilobytes?
questions.solution:
Capacity = 100 [latex]\times[/latex] 10 [latex]\times[/latex] 10 [latex]\times[/latex] 128 = 1,280,000 bytes.

In KB: 1,280,000 / 1024 = 1250 KB

Answer: 1250
